Common Deployment Issues
Issue #1: Azure Function App timeout errors
Cause: Default timeout is 5 minutes, some agents take longer on a cold start
Fix: Raise functionTimeout in rapp_ai/host.json and republish. A portal edit is overwritten by the next deployment.
Issue #2: Copilot Studio can't reach Azure Function
Cause: Rarely CORS. The template already deploys allowedOrigins ["*"], so Copilot Studio reaches the Function without further work.
Fix: Check the Function is running and the key is right first. Narrow allowedOrigins to your own origins before production.
Issue #3: Agents not loading (File Storage connection error)
Cause: The Function App managed identity is missing a storage role assignment. The storage account disallows shared keys, so no connection string can work.
Fix: Confirm the storage roles in azuredeploy.json are assigned to the Function App system-assigned identity.

sections.heading: Deployment Process (2-Step Setup)
sections.text:
Step 7.1: Deploy Azure Infrastructure
Use the Azure ARM template to create all required resources with one click:
Example: One-Click Azure Deployment
- Go to the repository: microsoft/aibast-agents-library
- Click the Deploy to Azure button in the README, which provisions from azuredeploy.json
- ARM template creates:
- Azure Function App (stateless intelligence layer)
- Azure File Storage (agent code + user memory)
- Application Insights (logging and monitoring)
- All networking and security configs
- Deployment completes in 5-10 minutes
One-click deployment: The Azure ARM template automatically provisions all required Azure infrastructure - Function App, Storage, App Insights, networking, and security configurations - without requiring manual Azure portal navigation. The deployment is fully automated and customer-facing users don't need to understand the underlying infrastructure.
Step 7.2: Run Setup Script
Execute the bash/PowerShell script that configures the environment:
# Option 1: Local setup (for testing)
git clone https://github.com/microsoft/aibast-agents-library.git
cd aibast-agents-library
./deploy.sh # or deploy.ps1 on Windows
# Script installs:
# - Python dependencies
# - Azure SDK
# - Connects to Azure Function App
# - Uploads default agents (memory, email)
# Option 2: Cloud setup (GitHub Codespaces)
# Click "Open in Codespaces" button
# Runs automatically in cloud - no local install needed
Dynamic loading: The setup script automates the entire environment configuration process - downloading dependencies, installing Python packages, connecting to Azure services, and uploading default agents. It handles all the technical plumbing automatically, regardless of whether running locally or in cloud environments.
Step 7.3: Deploy Your Agents
Copy the approved agents from Step 6 into the deployment:
# Local deployment (VS Code)
1. Copy your 6-10 reviewed agent files
2. Paste into /agents directory
3. Right-click → "Deploy to Function App"
4. Select your Azure subscription
5. Deployment completes in 2-3 minutes
# Cloud deployment (drag-and-drop)
1. Open Azure Portal → Your Function App
2. Navigate to File Storage → /agents folder
3. Drag approved .py files directly into folder
4. Agents hot-load automatically (zero downtime)
Hot-Loading = Zero Downtime
The stateless architecture means you can update agents WITHOUT restarting the Function App. Drop new agent files into Azure File Storage, and they're available instantly.
Example: Retail customer route optimization agent updated during live demo in minutes - no service interruption.
Step 7.4: Connect to M365 Copilot Studio
Make your agents accessible through Teams, Outlook, and web chat:
- Download the Copilot Studio solution for your solution: solutions/<slug>/exports/<slug>-copilot-studio-solution.zip, with the deployment settings JSON beside it. One ships per published solution.
- Import to Power Platform:
- Go to copilotstudio.microsoft.com
- Select "Import solution"
- Upload the .zip file
- Configure environment variables (Azure Function URL, API key)
- Enable channels: Check boxes for Teams, Web, Outlook, etc.
- Publish: One-click publish to M365
M365 integration: The process involves downloading the pre-built Copilot Studio solution, importing it into Power Platform, configuring the desired channels (Teams, Web, Outlook), and publishing - which exposes the agents across all Microsoft 365 interfaces where users work.
Example: Banking Customer Service Bot Deployment
Deployed agents: CheckIn, Onboarding, Research, Risk, Scheduler (6 agents total)
Deployment time: 45 minutes from code review approval to live in Teams
Process:
- Azure ARM template deployed → 8 minutes
- Setup script run → 5 minutes
- 6 agents uploaded to /agents folder → 2 minutes
- Copilot Studio solution imported → 10 minutes
- Teams channel enabled and tested → 20 minutes
Result: Customer can now chat with banker bot in Teams and test all 6 MVP scenarios

sections.heading: Testing Before Customer Demo
sections.text:
Role-play the MVP scenarios to ensure everything works:
Example: Rehearsal Testing (Banking Customer)
Scenario 1: Customer Check-In
You: "Hi, I'm here for my 2pm appointment"
Bot: *calls CheckInAgent*
Bot: "Welcome back! I see you're scheduled with your advisor at 2pm for account review. They'll be right with you."
✓ Verify: CheckInAgent logs show correct customer lookup
Scenario 2: Research 529 Plans
You: "I'd like to understand what 529 options are available"
Bot: *calls ResearchAgent*
Bot: "We offer three 529 college savings plans: [details]. Would you like me to compare them?"
✓ Verify: ResearchAgent returns relevant financial product info
Scenario 3: Open New Account
You: "Great, let's open an account"
Bot: *calls OnboardingAgent*
Bot: "I'll help you get started. First, let me verify your information..."
✓ Verify: OnboardingAgent initiates correct workflow
Real example: "So this is the use case for [Banking Customer]. So I basically loaded in those agents... And my prototyper is so good, you can basically rehearse with it."
What to check during rehearsal:
- Correct agent calls: LLM selects the right agent for each request
- Parameters passed correctly: Agent receives proper input (customer ID, date, etc.)
- Response quality: Agent returns useful, formatted output
- Error handling: Try invalid inputs - does it fail gracefully?
- Memory works: Bot remembers context across conversation

sections.heading: Optional: IT Firewall Testing
sections.text:
For security-sensitive customers, you can run the prototype locally:
# Run on single IT laptop (no cloud deployment needed)
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
# Start local Azure Function
func start
# Prototype runs on localhost:7071
# Customer can test without any data leaving their network
Security option: "It could run locally, so they don't even need to really hook it into their systems. You know, they could firewall it to one person's laptop in IT."

explain.title: Step 07 Deploy Prototype
explain.markdown:
# Step 07 Deploy Prototype

**Deploying the prototype** means getting the reviewed agents to answer real questions.
Locally there is nothing to deploy: install the Brainstem, drop the files in its agents folder, and ask.
Move to **Azure Functions** and **Copilot Studio** when the customer needs access without your laptop.

Guide section: [Step 7 in the production guide](../rapp-guide.html#step7)

## At a glance

- **Type:** Manual
- **Duration:** minutes locally; 1-2 hours for the cloud tiers, with scripts
- **Owner:** Technical Team
- **Input:** approved agents from [[Step 06 Code Quality Review]], project JSON, integration notes, the `microsoft/aibast-agents-library` repository
- **Output:** a working prototype reachable from Teams or web chat, verified before the demo

## The cloud path

### 7.1 Deploy Azure infrastructure

Use the **Deploy to Azure** button in the repository README. It provisions from `azuredeploy.json`:

- Azure Function App (stateless intelligence layer)
- Azure File Storage (agent code and user memory)
- Application Insights
- Networking and security configuration

It completes in 5-10 minutes.

### 7.2 Run the setup script

```
git clone https://github.com/microsoft/aibast-agents-library.git
cd aibast-agents-library
./deploy.sh # or deploy.ps1 on Windows
```

### 7.3 Deploy your agents

Copy the approved `.py` files into the agents location: deploy from VS Code, or drag them into the File Storage `agents` folder.
Agents **hot-load** with no restart. In Azure they refresh within five minutes.

### 7.4 Connect to Copilot Studio

1. Download `solutions/<slug>/exports/<slug>-copilot-studio-solution.zip` and its deployment settings JSON.
2. Import the solution in Copilot Studio.
3. Set environment variables (Function URL, API key).
4. Enable channels: Teams, Web, Outlook.
5. Publish.

## Verification checklist

| Check | How | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Function App running | Portal → Overview | Status "Running" |
| Agents loaded | File Storage → agents folder | Your `.py` files |
| Function responds | POST to Function URL | Lists available agents |
| Copilot Studio connected | Test chat | Replies to "Hello" |
| Agent calls work | Ask for one agent | Agent runs, returns result |
| Memory persists | Tell it something, ask later | It remembers |

## Common issues

- **Timeouts:** raise `functionTimeout` in `rapp_ai/host.json` and republish. A portal edit is overwritten by the next deployment.
- **Copilot Studio can't reach the Function:** rarely CORS. Check the Function is running and the key is right. Narrow `allowedOrigins` before production.
- **Agents not loading:** the Function App managed identity is missing a storage role. The storage account disallows shared keys, so no connection string will work.

## Rehearse before the demo

Role-play every MVP scenario. Check that:

- The model picks the **right agent** for each request.
- **Parameters** arrive correctly.
- Responses are useful and well formatted.
- **Invalid inputs fail gracefully.**
- Memory works across messages.

Then move to [[Step 08 Demo Review]].

## How rapp/1 underpins this step

- **One endpoint to test.** Every channel reaches the agents through the same wire: `POST /chat` with `user_input`, answering with `response`, `agent_logs` and `session_id`. `GET /health` is the liveness probe (§8). See [[The Wire]].
- **Deploying agents does not change the kernel.** New behavior lives outside the pinned Grail kernel (§11.1). Hot-loading agent files is that rule in practice. See [[The Brainstem Kernel]] and [[Distros and Pinning]].
- **Later stages.** Qualified releases and progressive rollout to production are covered by [[RAPP CICD]] and [[RAPP Deploy]], used from [[Step 13 Production Deployment]].
